source_text: Παντὶ δόγματι καὶ λόγῳ τῆς ἐν τοῖς οὖσιν ἀληθείας ἐχομένῳ παραφύεταί τι ψεῦδος· παραφύεται δὲ οὐκ ἐξ ὑποκειμένης τινὸς ἀρχῆς κατὰ φύσιν ὁρμώμενον ἢ τῆς κατ᾿ αὐτὸ ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἕκαστον αἰτίας, ἀλλ᾿ ὑπὸ τῶν τὴν ἔκθεσμον σπορὰν ἐπὶ διαφθορᾷ τῆς ἀληθείας τετιμηκότων σπουδαζόμενον. Τοῦτο δ᾿ ἔστιν εὑρεῖν πρῶτον μὲν ἐκ τῶν πάλαι ταῖς περὶ τούτων φροντίσιν ἐσχολακότων καὶ τῆς ἐκείνων πρός τε τοὺς ἑαυτῶν πρεσβυτέρους καὶ τοὺς ὁμοχρόνους γενομένης διαφορᾶς, οὐχ ἥκιστα δὲ ἐξ αὐτῆς τῆς τῶν ἐν μέσῳ στρεφομένων ταραχῆς. Οὐδὲν γὰρ τῶν ἀληθῶν οἱ τοιοῦτοι κατέλιπον ἀσυκοφάντητον, οὐ τὴν οὐσίαν τοῦ θεοῦ, οὐ τὴν γνῶσιν, οὐ τὴν ἐνέργειαν, οὐ τὰ τούτοις ἐφεξῆς καθ᾿ εἱρμὸν ἑπόμενα καὶ τὸν τῆς εὐσεβείας ἡμῖν ὑπογράφοντα λόγον. Ἀλλ᾿ οἱ μὲν πάντη καὶ καθάπαξ ἀπογινώσκουσι τὴν περὶ τούτων ἀλήθειαν, οἱ δὲ πρὸς τὸ δοκοῦν αὐτοῖς διαστρέφουσιν, οἱ δὲ καὶ περὶ τῶν ἐμφανῶν ἀπορεῖν ἐπιτηδεύουσιν. Ὅθεν οἶμαι δεῖν τοῖς περὶ ταῦτα πονουμένοις λόγων διττῶν, τῶν ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας, τῶν δὲ περὶ τῆς ἀληθείας· καὶ τῶν μὲν ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας πρὸς τοὺς ἀπιστοῦντας ἢ τοὺς ἀμφιβάλλοντας, τῶν δὲ περὶ τῆς ἀληθείας πρὸς τοὺς εὐγνωμονοῦντας καὶ μετ᾿ εὐνοίας δεχομένους τὴν ἀλήθειαν. Ὧν ἕνεκεν χρὴ τοὺς περὶ τούτων ἐξετάζειν ἐθέλοντας τὴν ἑκάστοτε προκειμένην χρείαν σκοπεῖν καὶ ταύτῃ τοὺς λόγους μετρεῖν, τήν τε περὶ τούτων τάξιν μεθαρμόζειν πρὸς τὰ δέον, καὶ μὴ τῷ δοκεῖν τὴν αὐτὴν πάντοτε φυλάττειν ἀρχὴν ἀμελεῖν τοῦ προσήκοντος καὶ τῆς ἐπιβαλλούσης ἑκάστῳ χώρας. Ὡς μὲν γὰρ πρὸς ἀπόδειξιν καὶ τὴν φυσικὴν ἀκολουθίαν, πάντοτε πρωτοστατοῦσιν οἱ περὶ αὐτῆς λόγοι τῶν ὑπὲρ αὐτῆς, ὡς δὲ πρὸς τὸ χρειωδέστερον, ἀνεστραμμένως οἱ ὑπὲρ αὐτῆς τῶν περὶ αὐτῆς. Οὔτε γὰρ γεωργὸς δύναιτ᾿ ἂν προσηκόντως καταβάλλειν τῇ γῇ τὰ σπέρματα, μὴ προεξελὼν τὰ τῆς ἀγρίας ὕλης καὶ τοῖς καταβαλλομένοις· ἡμέροις σπέρμασι λυμαινόμενα, οὔτε ἰατρὸς ἐνεῖναι τι τῶν ὑγιεινῶν φαρμάκων τῷ δεομένῳ θεραπείας σώματι, μὴ τὴν ἐνοῦσαν κακίαν προκαθήρας ἢ τὴν ἐπιῤῥέουσαν ἐπισχών· οὔτε μὴν ὁ τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἐθέλων διδάσκειν, περὶ τῆς ἀληθείας λέγων, πεῖσαι δύναιτ᾿ ἄν τινα ψευδοδοξίας τινὸς ὑποικουρούσης τῇ τῶν ἀκουόντων διανοίᾳ καὶ τοῖς λόγοις ἀντιστατούσης. Διὸ πρὸς τὸ χρειωδέστερον ἀφορῶντες καὶ ἡμεῖς προτάσσομεν ἔσθ᾿ ὅτε τοὺς ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας λόγους τῶν περὶ τῆς ἀληθείας· κατὰ τὸν αὐτὸν δὲ τρόπον ποιῆσαι καὶ νῦν ἐπὶ τῶν τῆς ἀναστάσεως λόγων οὐκ ἀχρεῖον φαίνεται σκοποῦσι τὸ δέον. Καὶ γὰρ ἐν τούτοις εὑρίσκομεν τοὺς μὲν ἀπιστοῦντας πάντη, τινὰς δὲ ἀμφιβάλλοντας, καὶ τῶν γε τὰς πρώτας ὑποθέσεις δεξαμένων τινὰς ἐπ᾿ ἴσης τοῖς ἀμφιβάλλουσιν ἀποροῦντας· τὸ δὲ πάντων παραλογώτατον ὅτι ταῦτα πάσχουσιν, οὐδ᾿ ἡντιναοῦν ἔχοντες ἐκ τῶν πραγμάτων ἀπιστίας ἀφορμήν, οὐδ᾿ αἰτίαν εὑρίσκοντες εἰπεῖν εὔλογον, δι᾿ ἣν ἀπιστοῦσιν ἢ διαποροῦσιν.
thought_title: Introduction to the Resurrection of the Dead
pass_a_gloss: To every doctrine and word of the truth in the things that are, some falsehood is added; and it is added not from some underlying natural principle or from the cause of the thing itself, but from those who have sown the seed of corruption of the truth in a disorderly manner. This is to find first from the ancients who were concerned with these matters and from the difference that arose between them and their predecessors and contemporaries, and not least from the turmoil of the things that are in the middle. For the people of this sort have left nothing of the true things uncalumniated, not the substance of God, not the knowledge, not the activity, not the things that follow these in order, and the word that outlines piety for us. But some people utterly and completely deny the truth about these things, some people distort it to their own opinion, and some people even pretend to be at a loss about the obvious things. From which I think it is necessary for those who are working on these things to use twofold words, some in defense of the truth and some about the truth; and some in defense of the truth against those who disbelieve or doubt, and some about the truth for those who are grateful and receive the truth with goodwill. For the sake of which it is necessary for those who want to examine these things to consider the particular need at hand and to measure their words by this, and to rearrange the order of these things according to what is necessary, and not to neglect the suitable and the pressing need of each thing because of the opinion that the same principle is always to be kept. For just as in the case of proof and natural sequence, the words in defense of the truth always take precedence over the words about the truth, but in the case of what is more necessary, the words in defense of the truth are reversed in relation to the words about the truth. For neither can a farmer properly sow the seeds in the earth without first clearing away the wild material and preparing the soil for what is to be sown; nor can a doctor administer any of the healthy medicines to the body that needs treatment without first removing the existing evil or checking the flowing one; nor can the person who wants to teach the truth, speaking about the truth, persuade anyone who is under the influence of some false opinion that is opposed to the thoughts and words of the listeners. Therefore, looking to what is more necessary, we also propose that sometimes the words in defense of the truth take precedence over the words about the truth; and it seems not unhelpful to do the same thing now in the case of the words about the resurrection, considering what is necessary. And indeed, we find among these people some who utterly disbelieve, some who doubt, and some who, even though they have accepted the initial hypotheses, are at a loss like those who doubt; and the most irrational thing of all is that they suffer these things without having any basis for their disbelief from the facts, and without finding any reasonable cause to say why they disbelieve or doubt.

choices.why: the verb παραφύεταί means to add or attach something
the preposition ὑπὲρ means in defense of or on behalf of
the preposition περὶ means about or concerning
the verb ἀπιστοῦντας means to disbelieve
the verb ἀμφιβάλλοντας means to doubt

pass_b_english: A falsehood attaches itself to every doctrine and word of the truth that exists in the things that are. This falsehood does not spring from some underlying natural principle or from the cause inherent in each thing itself; rather, it is promoted by those who have sown the seed of the truth's corruption in a disorderly manner. We discover this first from the ancients who devoted themselves to these inquiries and from the disagreements that arose among them, both with their predecessors and their contemporaries, and not least from the turmoil surrounding the matters currently in dispute. For people of this sort have left nothing true uncalumniated: not the substance of God, not the knowledge, not the activity, not the things that follow these in orderly sequence, and not the word that outlines piety for us. Some utterly and completely deny the truth about these matters; some distort it to fit their own opinion; some even pretend to be at a loss concerning the obvious. Therefore, I think those who labor over these things must employ a twofold discourse: words in defense of the truth, and words about the truth. The words in defense of the truth address those who disbelieve or doubt; the words about the truth address those who are fair-minded and receive the truth with goodwill. Consequently, anyone who wishes to examine these matters must consider the particular need at hand and measure their words by it, rearranging the order of treatment to suit the occasion, and not neglect the suitable and pressing need of each case because of the opinion that the same principle must always be kept. For just as, with respect to proof and natural sequence, words in defense of the truth always take precedence over words about the truth, so, with respect to what is more necessary, the words in defense of the truth are reversed in priority over the words about the truth. For neither can a farmer properly sow seeds in the earth without first clearing away the wild growth and preparing the ground for what is to be sown, nor can a doctor administer any healthy medicine to a body needing treatment without first purging the existing evil or staunching the flowing one; nor can the person who wants to teach the truth, by speaking about the truth, persuade anyone who labors under a false opinion that occupies the listeners' minds and opposes the words spoken. Therefore, looking to what is more necessary, we also propose that sometimes the words in defense of the truth take precedence over the words about the truth; and it seems not unhelpful to do the same thing now in the case of the words about the resurrection, considering what is required. Indeed, among these people we find some who utterly disbelieve, some who doubt, and some who, even though they have accepted the initial hypotheses, are at a loss just like those who doubt. The most irrational thing of all is that they suffer these things without having any basis for their disbelief from the facts, and without finding any reasonable cause to say why they disbelieve or doubt.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, particularly the distinction between 'ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας' (in defense of the truth) and 'περὶ τῆς ἀληθείας' (about the truth), which is central to the author's methodological argument. The analogies of the farmer and the doctor are rendered faithfully. No omissions or contradictions were found.
